prompt: A team is applying the Reliability pillar to a Bedrock-based application that calls foundation models. Which TWO patterns improve resilience to FM call failures and regional issues? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Disable retries to reduce latency
Increase the model temperature to add response variety
Implement circuit breakers in an AWS Step Functions workflow that stop calling the FM when error rates spike
Configure cross-Region failover so requests shift to a healthy Region
Store all prompts in a single Amazon S3 bucket in one Region

explanation: Circuit breakers prevent cascading failures by halting calls to a failing dependency. Cross-Region failover keeps the workload available during a regional impairment. Not "Disable retries to reduce latency": Removing retries reduces, not improves, resilience to transient failures. Not "Increase the model temperature to add response variety": Temperature affects output randomness, not reliability. Not "Store all prompts in a single Amazon S3 bucket in one Region": A single-Region store is a single point of failure, the opposite of resilient design. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/generative-ai-lens/generative-ai-lens.html

prompt: A platform team wants to track and attribute Bedrock inference costs per internal team while using cross-Region inference. Which capability lets them tag usage for cost tracking?

options.text: Provisioned Throughput model units
System-defined inference profiles, which you create and tag yourself
Application inference profiles, which are user-created and support tagging for cost allocation
AWS Cost Anomaly Detection profiles

explanation: Application inference profiles are custom profiles you create and tag, enabling cost tracking; system-defined profiles are AWS-managed. Not "Provisioned Throughput model units": Model Units reserve capacity; they are not the per-team tagging mechanism for cross-Region inference. Not "System-defined inference profiles, which you create and t…": System-defined profiles are predefined by AWS and are not user-tagged; application profiles are the taggable, custom ones. Not "AWS Cost Anomaly Detection profiles": That detects spend anomalies; it does not create taggable inference routing profiles. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-cards.html

prompt: A team must deploy existing Python agent code to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime with minimal overhead. It must auto-handle the HTTP server, /invocations and /ping endpoints, and support both sub-second and streaming responses. Which TWO approaches fit best? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Hand-build a FastAPI server with custom /invocations and /ping and your own container orchestration
Deploy on a SageMaker real-time endpoint with a custom inference container
Deploy on Amazon ECS Fargate with a fully custom container image and task definitions
Use the AgentCore starter toolkit to package, containerize (ARM64), push to ECR, and deploy
Use the AgentCore SDK with the @app.entrypoint decorator to auto-create the server and required endpoints

explanation: The starter toolkit automates packaging, container build, ECR push, and CreateAgentRuntime deployment. The SDK auto-creates an HTTP server (port 8080), implements /invocations and /ping, and supports JSON and streaming responses. Not "Hand-build a FastAPI server with custom /invocations and …": Manual FastAPI/Docker/orchestration adds the overhead AgentCore is meant to remove. Not "Deploy on a SageMaker real-time endpoint with a custom in…": A custom inference container adds infrastructure work AgentCore avoids. Not "Deploy on Amazon ECS Fargate with a fully custom containe…": Custom ECS deployment increases operational overhead versus AgentCore's managed flow. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents.html

prompt: An education company built a content generation system on Amazon Bedrock that generates practice questions from a mix of curated and scraped data. Reviewers must verify content credibility, so the company wants to add source lineage. Which combination of steps meets this with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker Clarify to explain model predictions
Register the curated and scraped input datasets with AWS Glue Data Catalog
Use AWS CloudTrail to log reviewer feedback actions
Tag FM outputs with metadata from the data source
Enable Amazon Bedrock invocation logging and correlate logs with the data source

explanation: The Data Catalog creates a searchable, managed inventory of sources with minimal overhead. Tagging outputs with source metadata gives reviewers direct, automated traceability between generated content and its origin. Not "Use Amazon SageMaker Clarify to explain model predictions": Clarify is for explainability/bias, not source lineage. Not "Use AWS CloudTrail to log reviewer feedback actions": CloudTrail logs API actions, not content source lineage. Not "Enable Amazon Bedrock invocation logging and correlate lo…": Correlating logs to sources requires manual or custom work and does not directly establish lineage. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler.html

prompt: A third-party application needs secure authentication to use Amazon Bedrock: integrate the existing IdP, keep audit logs, eliminate long-lived credentials, and provide temporary access. Which TWO solutions meet these requirements? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Create IAM users per employee and rotate keys with Secrets Manager
Use Amazon Cognito with OIDC to authenticate via the IdP and exchange tokens for temporary AWS credentials
Use an API Gateway Lambda authorizer validating against LDAP and issuing JWTs
Deploy AWS IAM Identity Center with SAML federation to the IdP and grant Bedrock via permission sets
Create an IAM role with STS AssumeRole but store IAM user credentials in app config

explanation: Cognito OIDC federates the IdP, issues temporary credentials, and audits via CloudTrail. IAM Identity Center with SAML federates the IdP, uses temporary credentials, and logs via CloudTrail. Not "Create IAM users per employee and rotate keys with Secret…": IAM users use long-lived keys and do not federate the IdP. Not "Use an API Gateway Lambda authorizer validating against L…": Custom LDAP/JWT does not provide temporary AWS credentials or native IdP federation. Not "Create an IAM role with STS AssumeRole but store IAM user…": Storing IAM user credentials violates the no-long-lived-credentials requirement. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/security.html

prompt: A Bedrock RAG app retrieves many relevant docs, but the most relevant info often appears lower in results. Which TWO steps improve relevance ranking with MINIMAL operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use Knowledge Bases with hybrid search and OpenSearch Serverless to combine vectors with keyword matching
Configure OpenSearch Serverless with Learning to Rank for relevance scoring
Create Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector and a custom similarity scoring algorithm
Use SageMaker JumpStart FMs with Kendra Intelligent Ranking and custom relevancy algorithms
Use Amazon Bedrock reranker models with Amazon OpenSearch Service to reorder results by semantic relevance

explanation: Hybrid search improves retrieval relevance by blending semantic and keyword matching. Bedrock rerankers are purpose-built to reorder results so the most relevant surface first. Not "Configure OpenSearch Serverless with Learning to Rank for…": Learning to Rank requires custom trained/maintained models — more overhead. Not "Create Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector and a custom simil…": Custom scoring and DB management add operational overhead. Not "Use SageMaker JumpStart FMs with Kendra Intelligent Ranki…": Bedrock built-in reranking is simpler and more integrated than custom ranking. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-chunking.html

prompt: A diagnostic imaging app must run similarity searches across 50 million images, processed daily but searched infrequently, with a cost-effective, responsive, no-infrastructure solution. Which is MOST cost-effective?

options.text: Store vectors in RDS for PostgreSQL with pgvector
Store vectors in Amazon OpenSearch Serverless and use vector search
Use DynamoDB to store vectors and custom similarity logic in Lambda
Create an Amazon S3 vector bucket with vector indexes to store image embeddings and perform similarity searches

explanation: S3 Vectors is serverless, scales to billions of vectors, and is cost-optimized for infrequent searches. Not "Store vectors in RDS for PostgreSQL with pgvector": RDS requires managing instances and is not cost-effective for infrequent workloads. Not "Store vectors in Amazon OpenSearch Serverless and use vec…": OpenSearch Serverless suits frequent low-latency search; provisioned capacity is underused for rare searches. Not "Use DynamoDB to store vectors and custom similarity logic…": DynamoDB has no native vector search; custom logic adds latency and cost. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base.html

prompt: A financial company needs Bedrock prompt templates governed via approval workflows and comprehensive logging of all model invocations with 7-year retention. Which TWO steps meet this with MINIMAL overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Enable CloudTrail data events for all Bedrock APIs into CloudTrail Lake with 7-year retention
Use EventBridge to capture invocation events to CloudWatch Logs then export to S3 Object Lock
Use Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management with multi-stage approval workflows and IAM multi-party authorization
Enable Bedrock model invocation logging to S3 with S3 Object Lock (compliance mode) for 7 years, with per-business-unit prefixes
Store prompt templates in DynamoDB with item-level permissions for approvals

explanation: Prompt Management natively handles versioned templates with multi-stage approvals. Invocation logging plus immutable Object Lock storage meets comprehensive 7-year retention with low overhead. Not "Enable CloudTrail data events for all Bedrock APIs into C…": CloudTrail captures API metadata, not full prompt/response content. Not "Use EventBridge to capture invocation events to CloudWatc…": Custom pipelines add failure points and do not provide a complete audit trail. Not "Store prompt templates in DynamoDB with item-level permis…": Custom approval logic in DynamoDB adds development overhead. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-management.html

prompt: A DJL-served LLM on 8-GPU instances is underutilized: real max sequence length is 10x smaller than configured, concurrency is low, and the model fits within 4 GPUs. Which TWO steps improve resource utilization? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Increase the number of instances and spread requests more evenly
Use tensor parallelism degree 8 to split the model across all GPUs
Use tensor parallelism with a degree of 4 to deploy two model replicas per instance
Enable speculative decoding to reduce per-request latency
Reduce the model's maximum sequence length to allow a higher rolling batch size per GPU

explanation: Since the model fits in 4 GPUs, degree 4 packs two replicas across 8 GPUs for full utilization. Freeing memory by lowering max sequence length increases batch size, throughput, and concurrency. Not "Increase the number of instances and spread requests more…": This does not raise per-instance concurrency or reduce the memory footprint. Not "Use tensor parallelism degree 8 to split the model across…": Degree 8 serves only one replica across 8 GPUs, leaving half idle since the model fits in 4. Not "Enable speculative decoding to reduce per-request latency": Speculative decoding improves latency, not utilization. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/deploy-model.html

prompt: A company is developing a RAG application on Amazon Bedrock that processes customer support documents. The application retrieves many relevant documents, but users report that the most relevant information often appears lower in the results. The company wants to improve relevance ranking so the most useful information appears first. Which combination of steps will improve relevance with MINIMAL operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker JumpStart FMs with Amazon Kendra Intelligent Ranking to create custom relevancy scoring algorithms.
Use Knowledge Bases with hybrid search and Amazon OpenSearch Serverless to combine vector embeddings with keyword matching.
Configure Amazon OpenSearch Serverless with the Bedrock Knowledge Bases plugin and use OpenSearch Learning to Rank for relevance scoring.
Create an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database with pgvector and a custom similarity scoring algorithm combining vector distances with metadata.
Use Amazon Bedrock reranker models with Amazon OpenSearch Service to reorder retrieved results based on semantic relevance to the query.

explanation: Hybrid search combines semantic vector embeddings with keyword matching to improve retrieval relevance with minimal overhead. Bedrock reranker models are purpose-built to score query-document relevance and reorder results so the most relevant information appears first. Not "Use Amazon SageMaker JumpStart FMs with Amazon Kendra Int…": Bedrock already provides built-in reranking optimized for FM integration; this approach is more complex and less integrated. Not "Configure Amazon OpenSearch Serverless with the Bedrock K…": Learning to Rank is an open-source plugin that requires custom scoring and trained, maintained models — more overhead than built-in Bedrock features. Not "Create an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database with pgvector…": This requires custom development and managing the vector database — more operational overhead. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base.html

prompt: A financial services company runs a RAG application that answers questions from internal market analysis reports. It uses an Amazon Bedrock embedding model and an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster as the vector store; a Lambda function performs embedding and search. After a code update, the app returns generic responses such as 'no relevant information found' even for previously answerable questions. CloudWatch Logs shows no errors, X-Ray confirms successful FM invocation, the cluster is healthy, and query latency is normal. What is the cause of this issue?

options.text: The Amazon Bedrock FM temperature parameter was increased.
The Lambda function's IAM role is missing bedrock:InvokeModel permission.
The document embeddings in OpenSearch were deleted during the update and not re-indexed.
The updated Lambda function uses a different version of the embedding model.

explanation: Embedding drift: query embeddings generated by a different model than was used to index documents cause a vector-space mismatch and ineffective retrieval. Not "The Amazon Bedrock FM temperature parameter was increased.": Temperature affects generation randomness, not retrieval; this is a retrieval failure. Not "The Lambda function's IAM role is missing bedrock:InvokeM…": The model is invoked successfully; a missing permission would throw an access error. Not "The document embeddings in OpenSearch were deleted during…": Deleted embeddings would surface in logs or failed queries; with no errors and normal latency, documents are still being retrieved. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-chunking.html

prompt: A financial services company wants a mobile app to help users with account inquiries and general account information. It has a large volume of customer-support email exchanges to use as source material, stored in Amazon S3. The data contains personally identifiable information (PII) that must not appear in search results. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Comprehend to detect and redact PII from the email data in S3, and integrate Comprehend with Amazon Kendra to enable enterprise search of the processed data.
Use Amazon Kendra for enterprise search and integrate with an Amazon Bedrock FM, using a system prompt to identify and remove PII during query processing.
Use Amazon Comprehend to detect and redact PII, and integrate with Amazon DocumentDB for database queries.
Use Amazon Textract to extract text, Amazon Macie to scan for PII in S3, and integrate Textract and S3 with Amazon Kendra.

explanation: Comprehend detects and redacts PII from text, and Kendra provides managed enterprise search over the processed data for conversational integration. Not "Use Amazon Kendra for enterprise search and integrate wit…": System prompts cannot reliably or consistently remove PII and can be jailbroken — not secure for sensitive financial data. Not "Use Amazon Comprehend to detect and redact PII, and integ…": DocumentDB requires custom search development and lacks NLP for natural-language interactions; it is not enterprise search. Not "Use Amazon Textract to extract text, Amazon Macie to scan…": Macie is for data discovery/security posture, not PII redaction for GenAI; Textract targets scanned documents, not raw email text. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock.html

prompt: A company wants an application that analyzes videos and photos from public fashion shows to understand style elements and trends, stores the extracted information, and provides a dashboard summarizing trends. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Use AWS Step Functions to process videos and photos with Amazon Bedrock multimodal FMs, store results in S3, and use an Amazon QuickSight dashboard to visualize trends.

Use Amazon EventBridge to trigger Lambda functions that use Amazon QuickSight Q to analyze the videos and photos, store results in S3, and deploy a QuickSight dashboard with ML-powered trend analysis.
Use an Anthropic Claude model in Bedrock to analyze text descriptions, use Stable Diffusion for image analysis, store results in OpenSearch Service, and create a Managed Grafana dashboard.
Use Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels to train a custom model, store results in DynamoDB, and create an Amazon Managed Grafana dashboard with custom plugins.

explanation: Bedrock multimodal FMs (e.g., Amazon Nova Pro, Claude) analyze visual content directly without custom model development; Step Functions orchestrates and QuickSight builds dashboards serverlessly. Not "Use Amazon EventBridge to trigger Lambda functions that u…": QuickSight Q answers questions about data already in a dashboard; it cannot analyze videos or photos. Not "Use an Anthropic Claude model in Bedrock to analyze text …": This manages an OpenSearch cluster and multiple FMs with custom visualizations, and analyzes text descriptions rather than the visual content directly. Not "Use Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels to train a custom mo…": This requires custom model training/maintenance and custom Grafana plugin development — more overhead. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-cards.html

prompt: A cross-functional team is developing a generative AI application on AWS. The team needs to optimize developer productivity, enforce consistent integration patterns, automate performance tuning, and accelerate AI testing across multiple business units using Amazon Q Developer while maintaining application quality. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use Amazon Q Developer to retrospectively analyze and document common integration patterns across business units' code bases.
Integrate Amazon Q Developer automated unit and integration test generation into the team's CI/CD pipelines.
Incorporate Amazon Q Developer to resolve coding issues during merge requests, reserving most refactoring and optimization for periodic manual review cycles.
Use Amazon Q Developer to analyze code for security best practices, with mandatory manual security-team approval of all code changes before integration.
Configure Amazon Q Developer to automatically generate and refactor integration code, provide targeted API usage guidance, and suggest performance optimizations across the modular code base.

explanation: Embedding automated test generation into CI/CD continuously validates components, sustaining velocity and quality with early defect detection. This delivers real-time code generation, refactoring, API recommendations, and performance optimization, increasing productivity and reducing integration errors. Not "Use Amazon Q Developer to retrospectively analyze and doc…": Reactive retrospective analysis fails to use real-time assistance for generation, refactoring, and testing. Not "Incorporate Amazon Q Developer to resolve coding issues d…": Limiting use to merge/review stages and infrequent manual cycles does not optimize the core benefits. Not "Use Amazon Q Developer to analyze code for security best …": Mandatory manual approval of all changes creates a bottleneck and does not accelerate workflows or automate tuning/testing. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonq/latest/qdeveloper-ug/what-is.html

prompt: A company runs a question-answering application that uses an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base ingesting documents from multiple Amazon S3 buckets. The company needs to monitor the data ingestion process to identify and troubleshoot document-processing issues. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Implement Amazon Bedrock model invocation logging to capture metrics about document processing and embedding generation.
Enable Amazon CloudWatch Application Signals to automatically detect and alert on knowledge base performance issues.
Configure knowledge base logging with Amazon CloudWatch Logs as the destination and use CloudWatch Logs Insights to query for failed document processing.
Enable AWS CloudTrail to track all API calls related to knowledge base operations and document ingestion.

explanation: Knowledge bases support built-in logging to CloudWatch Logs that records per-file ingestion status (ingested, ignored, failed); Logs Insights can query statuses such as RESOURCE_IGNORED, EMBEDDING_FAILED, or INDEXING_FAILED. Not "Implement Amazon Bedrock model invocation logging to capt…": Model invocation logging captures inference requests, not knowledge base ingestion processes. Not "Enable Amazon CloudWatch Application Signals to automatic…": Application Signals monitors application performance/health and does not integrate with knowledge base ingestion monitoring. Not "Enable AWS CloudTrail to track all API calls related to k…": CloudTrail tracks API calls but not the document-level processing information needed to troubleshoot ingestion. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-invocation-logging.html

prompt: A security team is hardening a Bedrock workload according to the Security pillar of the Generative AI Lens. Which TWO practices should they adopt? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Send prompts to a public endpoint without TLS to reduce overhead.
Embed long-lived IAM access keys in the application package.
Encrypt data at rest with AWS KMS and reach Bedrock through VPC endpoints to keep traffic on the AWS network.
Apply least-privilege IAM with condition keys (for example, requiring a specific bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier) for model access.
Disable all logging to minimize the data footprint.

explanation: Customer-managed encryption and private connectivity protect data confidentiality and reduce exposure of prompts and outputs. Least-privilege identity-based policies with condition keys restrict who can call models and can enforce that guardrails are applied. Not "Send prompts to a public endpoint without TLS to reduce o…": Unencrypted transport exposes sensitive prompt and response data. Not "Embed long-lived IAM access keys in the application package.": Long-lived embedded keys are a major security risk and violate credential best practices. Not "Disable all logging to minimize the data footprint.": Disabling logging removes the audit trail needed for security monitoring and compliance. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/generative-ai-lens/generative-ai-lens.html

prompt: A team is preparing a dataset to fine-tune a foundation model and wants to maximize resulting quality while avoiding overfitting and data leakage. Which TWO data-preparation steps best support these goals? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Include duplicate records to increase the dataset size.
Increase the number of training epochs regardless of validation loss.
Include PII in the examples to add more signal.
Hold out a separate validation/test split that does not overlap the training data.
Deduplicate and clean/normalize the examples.

explanation: A non-overlapping evaluation split prevents train/test leakage and gives an honest measure of generalization. Removing duplicates and normalizing inconsistent text reduces bias toward repeated samples and improves the signal the model learns from. Not "Include duplicate records to increase the dataset size.": Duplication inflates size artificially and encourages overfitting to repeated examples. Not "Increase the number of training epochs regardless of vali…": Blindly adding epochs is a training hyperparameter choice, not data preparation, and risks overfitting. Not "Include PII in the examples to add more signal.": Including PII creates privacy and compliance risk and does not improve task quality. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler.html

prompt: A team wants to A/B test two wordings of a production prompt and roll back instantly if one underperforms, without redeploying application code. Which Amazon Bedrock capability supports this?

options.text: Hard-code both prompts in the application and redeploy to switch.
Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management with versioned prompts and variants.
Store prompts in environment variables only.
Change the temperature parameter to switch prompts.

explanation: Prompt Management stores prompts as versioned, parameterized resources with variants, so teams can compare wordings and switch or roll back without code changes. Not "Hard-code both prompts in the application and redeploy to…": Hard-coding requires a code change and redeploy for every switch or rollback. Not "Store prompts in environment variables only.": Environment variables lack versioning, variants, and managed rollback for prompts. Not "Change the temperature parameter to switch prompts.": Temperature does not select between prompt wordings. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-management.html

prompt: An agent should ground its answers in the company's policy documents in addition to taking actions. With the LEAST custom code, how should the developer add this knowledge?

options.text: Associate an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base with the agent.
Fine-tune the agent's model on the policies each week.
Embed the entire policy library into the agent's instructions.
Store policies in DynamoDB and query them with custom code.

explanation: Associating a knowledge base lets the agent retrieve and ground responses on the documents without custom retrieval code. Not "Fine-tune the agent's model on the policies each week.": Repeated fine-tuning is heavy and unnecessary when a knowledge base provides current grounding. Not "Embed the entire policy library into the agent's instruct…": Instructions have limited size and cannot scale to a full document library or stay current. Not "Store policies in DynamoDB and query them with custom code.": A custom store and retrieval code adds work that the built-in knowledge base association avoids. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents.html

prompt: A team must retain the full request and response content of every Amazon Bedrock model call for troubleshooting and audit. Which capability captures this with the LEAST custom code?

options.text: Use Amazon Macie on the application logs.
Enable AWS CloudTrail only.
Add print statements in the application and hope they are captured.
Enable Amazon Bedrock model invocation logging to Amazon S3 (and/or CloudWatch Logs).

explanation: Model invocation logging is a built-in feature that records full prompts, responses, and metadata to S3 and/or CloudWatch with no custom instrumentation. Not "Use Amazon Macie on the application logs.": Macie classifies sensitive data; it does not capture model request/response content. Not "Enable AWS CloudTrail only.": CloudTrail records API activity metadata, not the full prompt and response content. Not "Add print statements in the application and hope they are…": Ad hoc logging is incomplete and unreliable compared with built-in invocation logging. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-invocation-logging.html

prompt: A production Bedrock workload has steady, high, predictable demand for 12 business hours and near-zero traffic overnight. The team must guarantee dedicated capacity during business hours (no throttling) at the lowest total cost, keeping the same model and API. Which approach is BEST?

options.text: Use Provisioned Throughput without a long-term commitment, creating model units for business hours and deleting them overnight.
Use on-demand inference for all traffic.
Use Provisioned Throughput with a 6-month commitment sized for peak.
Use cross-Region inference to add capacity during business hours.

explanation: No-commitment Provisioned Throughput guarantees dedicated capacity while active and is billed only while provisioned, so releasing units overnight avoids paying for the idle period. Not "Use on-demand inference for all traffic.": On-demand has no idle cost but cannot guarantee dedicated capacity during peak hours, so it fails the no-throttling requirement. Not "Use Provisioned Throughput with a 6-month commitment size…": A committed term is cheapest per hour but you pay for the reserved units overnight too, so with near-zero overnight traffic it is not the lowest total cost. Not "Use cross-Region inference to add capacity during busines…": Cross-Region inference spreads on-demand traffic for throughput/availability but does not reserve guaranteed capacity, and it is still on-demand priced. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/generative-ai-lens/generative-ai-lens.html

prompt: A bank's assistant must always cite the LATEST internal regulations (which change weekly) AND must CONSISTENTLY emit a strict report template. Which approach meets BOTH with the least ongoing effort?

options.text: Fine-tune the model every week on both the regulations and the template.
Use RAG only, relying on a detailed prompt to enforce the template.
Use continued pre-training on the regulations and a prompt for the template.
Use RAG for the frequently changing regulations and fine-tune the model for the fixed report template/style.

explanation: RAG keeps regulatory content current without retraining, while fine-tuning reliably enforces a rigid output format; each technique handles the part it is best at. Not "Fine-tune the model every week on both the regulations an…": Weekly fine-tuning is operationally heavy and still lags between runs; RAG handles freshness far more cheaply. Not "Use RAG only, relying on a detailed prompt to enforce the…": RAG fixes freshness, but prompt-only formatting is not reliably consistent, which the scenario explicitly requires. Not "Use continued pre-training on the regulations and a promp…": Continued pre-training is for absorbing domain language from large corpora, is heavy, and does not keep weekly content current. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-cards.html

prompt: A team needs human-labeled instruction/response pairs with a managed workforce option and built-in quality controls (annotation consolidation). Which service is BEST?

options.text: Amazon Comprehend custom classification.
Raw Amazon Mechanical Turk tasks.
Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler.
Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth.

explanation: Ground Truth provides managed labeling workflows, workforce options, and quality features such as annotation consolidation. Not "Amazon Comprehend custom classification.": Comprehend automates classification; it is not a human-labeling service for creating new pairs. Not "Raw Amazon Mechanical Turk tasks.": Mechanical Turk supplies a crowd but lacks the managed labeling workflow, templates, and consolidation that Ground Truth adds. Not "Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler.": Data Wrangler transforms tabular data; it does not run human annotation. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler.html

prompt: A Bedrock knowledge base needs a fully managed vector store for HIGH query-per-second, LOW-latency similarity search with no capacity planning. Which option is BEST?

options.text: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless.
Amazon Neptune Analytics.
Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector.
Amazon S3 Vectors.

explanation: OpenSearch Serverless is the natively integrated, auto-scaling managed vector store suited to frequent, low-latency queries without capacity planning. Not "Amazon Neptune Analytics.": Neptune Analytics powers GraphRAG over relationships, not general high-QPS vector search. Not "Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector.": Aurora pgvector is supported but you size and manage the database instance; it is not the auto-scaling serverless choice for high QPS. Not "Amazon S3 Vectors.": S3 Vectors optimizes cost for infrequent queries at huge scale, not high-QPS low-latency search. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base.html

prompt: A team wants to raise the overall quality of what their RAG system retrieves and answers. Which TWO techniques are most effective? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Choose a chunking strategy (semantic or hierarchical) aligned to the documents' structure.
Raise the generation temperature for variety.
Add a reranking step to reorder retrieved candidates by relevance.
Increase maxTokens on the response.
Always return only the single top result.

explanation: Structure-aligned chunking produces more coherent, relevant chunks and better retrieval. A reranker moves the most relevant passages to the top for generation. Not "Raise the generation temperature for variety.": Higher temperature increases randomness and does not improve retrieval quality. Not "Increase maxTokens on the response.": Output length does not change which passages are retrieved. Not "Always return only the single top result.": Returning just one result can drop relevant passages and reduce answer quality. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-chunking.html

prompt: A developer needs a MANAGED, low-code way to build and version a multi-step generative workflow with branching (classify, then retrieve, then generate). Which Amazon Bedrock feature is BEST?

options.text: Hand-built AWS Step Functions wiring each step.
Amazon Bedrock Agents.
A single InvokeModel call.
Amazon Bedrock Flows (prompt flows).

explanation: Bedrock Flows visually build and version multi-step, branching workflows chaining prompts, knowledge bases, and other components with little code. Not "Hand-built AWS Step Functions wiring each step.": Step Functions can orchestrate but require more custom build than a managed flow builder. Not "Amazon Bedrock Agents.": Agents provide autonomous tool-using reasoning, which is heavier and different from a defined, branching prompt-chain workflow. Not "A single InvokeModel call.": One call cannot orchestrate a multi-step, branching workflow. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-management.html

prompt: For compliance, the company's OWN application must execute tool calls, while the agent still decides which action to take. Which capability supports this?

options.text: Configure the action group to return control to the caller, which executes the action and returns the result.
Use an action group with a Lambda the agent invokes directly.
Disable the agent's reasoning.
Associate a knowledge base.

explanation: Return of control hands the chosen action and parameters back to the calling application to execute, rather than the agent invoking a Lambda. Not "Use an action group with a Lambda the agent invokes direc…": With a Lambda action group the agent executes the action, which is exactly what the compliance rule forbids. Not "Disable the agent's reasoning.": That would remove the agent's ability to decide which action to take. Not "Associate a knowledge base.": A knowledge base is for retrieval, not for delegating execution to the caller. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents.html

prompt: A team deploys several large language models to GPU instances and wants to pack multiple models/copies onto shared accelerators, scale each independently, and scale unused ones to ZERO. Which capability fits?

options.text: SageMaker inference components.
Serverless Inference.
One real-time endpoint per model.
A multi-model endpoint (MME).

explanation: Inference components place multiple models/copies on shared instances, allocate resources per component, scale independently, and can scale to zero. Not "Serverless Inference.": Serverless does not support the GPUs these LLMs need. Not "One real-time endpoint per model.": Separate endpoints cannot pack models onto shared accelerators with independent scaling. Not "A multi-model endpoint (MME).": MME loads many (typically smaller) models on demand behind one endpoint but is not designed for GPU-packing LLMs with independent per-model scaling and scale-to-zero. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/deploy-model.html

prompt: Invocation logs are stored in CloudWatch Logs, and an engineer must interactively query them to find and aggregate error patterns. Which tool is BEST?

options.text: AWS CloudTrail Lake.
Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights.
Amazon Athena with no setup.
Amazon QuickSight Q.

explanation: Logs Insights provides an interactive query language to search and aggregate the CloudWatch log data. Not "AWS CloudTrail Lake.": CloudTrail Lake queries CloudTrail API events, not arbitrary invocation logs already in CloudWatch Logs. Not "Amazon Athena with no setup.": Athena would require exporting and cataloging the data first; Logs Insights queries the logs directly. Not "Amazon QuickSight Q.": QuickSight Q answers over prepared BI datasets, not ad hoc CloudWatch log querying. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-invocation-logging.html

prompt: A compliance team must ensure customer prompts are processed only within an approved Region and are NOT used to train the base models. Which statement and action are correct?

options.text: Accept that data may be processed globally.
Self-host the model, since only that prevents base-model training on your data.
Use Bedrock in the approved Region; it processes the data in that Region and does not use your prompts/outputs to train the base models.
File a support ticket to opt out, or your data trains the models by default.

explanation: Bedrock keeps inference data in the Region you call and does not use customer inputs/outputs to train base models. Not "Accept that data may be processed globally.": Inference data is processed in the Region you invoke, not globally. Not "Self-host the model, since only that prevents base-model …": Using Bedrock already prevents your data from training base models; self-hosting is unnecessary for that guarantee. Not "File a support ticket to opt out, or your data trains the…": No opt-out is required; Bedrock does not use your data to train base models. Read more: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-identity.html
